text:
Tristan Jarry keeps getting the Oilers out of nights they had no business winning. The Edmonton Journal's headline after the Nov. 11 overtime win in Philadelphia said the Flyers dominated "but Tristan Jarry saves the day," and he followed it in the rematch with his best game of the season by our numbers. Across his last five starts he has saved 9.77 goals above expected, meaning he kept out that many more goals than the shots he faced would usually allow. For the season he is 6-1-3 with a .909 save rate and 3.3 goals saved above expected.

The season total hides a slow start: two six-goal games, against Vancouver and Toronto. The shape of his numbers is unusual. He has been below league average on low-danger shots (.945 against .963) and well above it on medium-danger ones. He is sharing the net, with 10 starts, and Daily Faceoff has praised both him and Devon Levi. The Hockey News reported that Mike Babcock wants "less goaltending heroics," which says as much about the team in front of him as it does about Jarry.
